title: Server checkpoint advisories and resumable window for SSE streams
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Clients reconnecting to long-running SSE streams can either request a coarse resume token (drop-and-resume) or attempt fine-grained reassembly using opaque tokens. This leads to trade-offs: long-lived requests can replay large amounts of data, and proxies/load-balancers may rewrite connections which breaks some resume strategies. We need a pragmatic server-driven advisory mechanism that reduces wasted retransmit work, is robust to intermediate proxies, and preserves tool/function-call atomicity and structured output boundaries.

Proposal: Implement server checkpoint advisories and a resumable window. Servers will emit lightweight 'checkpoint' events periodically (configurable cadence) that include: sequence_id, last_complete_logical_offset, optional canonical-hash, and an advisory_ttl (ms). Clients may use the most recent checkpoint to request a resume at or after the checkpoint offset. Crucially:
- Checkpoints are advisory only; servers may still permit resume at earlier offsets but can prefer heuristics that avoid expensive rehydration.
- Checkpoints include semantic boundary markers so function/tool-call events are not cut mid-call.
- For compatibility, checkpoints will be emitted as SSE events with event:type="checkpoint" and a minimal JSON payload. Framing will remain length-prefixed for data payloads but checkpoints will be newline-terminated JSON to be proxy-friendly.

Goals: Reduce retransmit across reconnects, make resumption robust against proxy rewrite (no long-lived binary tokens), preserve atomic function-call handoffs, and keep the client API ergonomic (only need to send back sequence_id + offset).
acceptance_criteria: Servers emit checkpoint events at the configured cadence under high-throughput and idle conditions.
Clients can resume from a checkpoint with a resume request containing sequence_id and offset and receive exactly-once semantics for structured function-call events (no partial tool-call replay).
Checkpoint payloads are compact (<512 bytes typical) and resilient when passed through HTTP intermediaries (no binary blobs).
End-to-end tests demonstrate reduced retransmit volume for simulated flapping clients by at least 60% compared to naive full-resume behavior.
Backward compatibility: older clients that ignore checkpoint events continue to work (no regressions).
implementation_notes:
Server: add checkpoint emitter in the runtime output path; minimal CPU work (snapshot of latest logical offset + boundary flags). Expose config: checkpoint_interval_ms, advisory_ttl_ms, include_hash boolean. Client: on reconnect include Resume-Sequence and Resume-Offset headers (or resume fields in JSON body for POST-based resume). If server replies with a mismatch (sequence_id unknown or expired), fallback to full-history replay with an opt-in backoff. Ensure SDKs map checkpoints to existing StreamSession objects.

Framing: standard SSE for control events; structured output chunks continue as length-prefixed JSON payloads. Checkpoints avoid base64/opaque tokens to prevent proxy mangling. Function calls: annotate checkpoint with last_complete_function_call_id to guarantee atomicity when resuming.

Telemetry: emit metrics for checkpoint_emitted, resume_attempts_using_checkpoint, resume_mismatches, retransmit_bytes_saved. Add dashboards and alerts if resume_mismatches > 1% over 5m.
test_plan: Unit tests for emitter and client parsing; integration tests that spawn an SSE server, stream structured outputs with interleaved function calls, simulate abrupt client disconnects and proxy-induced chunk reorders, then assert that resume from checkpoint produces no partial function-call deliveries. Load test with 10k concurrent streams to measure checkpoint overhead. Fuzz tests for malformed checkpoint payloads. Include backward compatibility test where client ignores checkpoint events. Put automated regression in CI gate for streaming-related releases.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Stage 1: runtime emits checkpoints behind flag and metrics enabled (internal alpha). Stage 2: SDKs add resume support and opt-in flag for clients. Stage 3: default enable for new streams, and opt-in for existing customers for 2 weeks, followed by default-on. Provide docs and migration notes. Monitor telemetry and roll back if RTT or error rate increases beyond threshold.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Proxies drop or coalesce SSE events producing checkpoint loss. Mitigation: include monotonically increasing sequence_id and short advisory_ttl so client can fall back to previous checkpoint or full resume.

Risk: Checkpointing increases server CPU for extremely high-throughput workloads. Mitigation: make checkpoint interval configurable and aggregated; emit checkpoints only when logical offset advanced beyond threshold.
Risk: Client resume semantics become inconsistent across SDKs. Mitigation: ship reference implementation in JS/Python SDKs and a compatibility test harness that all SDKs must pass.

Risk: Security/authorization issues if checkpoints leak across tenants. Mitigation: include tenant-scoped sequence_id and validate resume requests against auth tokens; require security review for private deployments.
